formats.key: CommitIntent(address user,address token,uint256 amount,bytes32 rulesHash,uint64 duration,uint256 fine,address recipient,uint256 nonce,uint256 deadline)
effects: Lets anyone submit the signed intent through commitWithSig until `deadline`. The submitter (msg.sender, e.g. the deposit-address forwarder) pays `amount` of `token` into the vault.
Opens a commitment owned by `user` (the signer). The signer gets any refund and is the only one who can call emergencyWithdraw.

Takes a platform fee at commit time: max(platformFeeBps of the deposit, which is 1% at deploy, minFeeUsd converted to token units through Chainlink, which is $1 at deploy). The fee is credited to the treasury, so the locked stake is the deposit minus the fee.
Locks the net stake for `duration` seconds under the off-chain rules in `rulesHash`. The oracle decides whether the rules were broken.

If the oracle rules a violation, `fine` is forfeited: forfeitFeeBps (15% at deploy) goes to the treasury and the rest to `recipient`, or all of it goes to the treasury when recipient == treasury. The signer gets back stake minus fine.
If there is no violation, the full net stake (deposit minus fee) goes back to the signer. If the oracle never resolves, the signer can emergency-withdraw it after endsAt plus a grace period.
Uses up the signer's commit nonce `nonce`. The commit reverts if fine > net stake, for example when fine equals amount.
formats.shown: "Open commitment", then the trader, the stake amount and slash penalty in the token, the duration, the slash recipient, an expiry date, the stake token, a raw rules hash and the nonce.

findings.title: CommitIntent: 'Stake amount' shows the gross deposit, but the platform fee is cut before the stake is locked.
findings.evidence: CommitmentVaultV4._commit: `uint256 fee = _computeFee(token, totalDeposit); ... uint256 netStake = totalDeposit - fee; ... _credit(token, treasury, fee);`. _computeFee is the larger of `totalDeposit * platformFeeBps / 10_000` (100 bps at deploy) and minFeeInToken (minFeeUsd = 1e8 = $1). Descriptor: field `amount` labelled 'Stake amount' with no mention of any fee. In case 0 the screen says 'Stake amount 10 USDC', but the locked and refundable stake is at most 9.9 USDC, or 9 USDC with the $1 floor.
findings.fix: Rename the field to 'Deposit (platform fee deducted)'. Have the intent say a fee is taken, e.g. 'Deposit tokens into a commitment (platform fee: 1% or $1 minimum)'.

findings.title: CommitIntent: 'Slash recipient' implies it gets the whole penalty; 15% goes to the treasury.
findings.evidence: CommitmentVaultV4._computeSlashShares: `toTreasury = (c.fine * forfeitFeeBps) / 10_000; toRecipient = c.fine - toTreasury;` (forfeitFeeBps = 1_500 at deploy). Descriptor fields: 'Slash penalty' (fine) and 'Slash recipient' (recipient). The signer's loss on a slash is the full fine, which is shown right. The named recipient only gets 85% of it.
findings.fix: Relabel to 'Slash recipient (after protocol share)', or name the treasury share in the intent.

findings.title: CommitIntent: the intent 'Open commitment' does not say tokens are staked and can be slashed; no interpolatedIntent.
findings.evidence: Descriptor: `"intent": "Open commitment"` and no interpolatedIntent. The code locks `amount` of `token` and lets the oracle forfeit `fine` to `recipient` (_applyResolution).
findings.fix: Add an interpolatedIntent such as 'Stake {amount} for {duration}; lose up to {fine} if rules are broken', and use an intent like 'Stake tokens in a slashable commitment'.

findings.title: CommitIntent: the user field allows only 'eoa', but the contract also accepts smart-account (EIP-1271) signers.
findings.evidence: CommitmentVaultV5.commitWithSig: `SignatureChecker.isValidSignatureNow(intent.user, digest, sig)` (ECDSA and EIP-1271). Descriptor: `user` params `types: ["eoa"]`.
findings.fix: Use `types: ["eoa", "contract"]`, or add `senderAddress`-style handling if the wallet supports it.

findings.title: CommitIntent case 0 signs fine == amount, which the contract always rejects after the fee.
findings.evidence: cases/0.json: amount 10000000, fine 10000000 (10 USDC each). CommitmentVaultV4._commit: `if (fine > netStake) revert InvalidFine(fine, netStake);` with netStake = amount - fee, and fee > 0. The test shows a commitment that cannot execute.
findings.fix: Use a fine at or below the net stake (e.g. amount 10 USDC, fine 5 USDC) so the case is a real, executable intent.

findings.title: CommitIntent: rulesHash stands for the off-chain rules that decide the slash, which no screen can show.
findings.evidence: CommitmentVaultV5.CommitIntent: `bytes32 rulesHash; // off-chain rule spec digest`. Descriptor: 'Rules hash' (raw).
findings.fix: None in the descriptor. The app should show the rules the hash commits to.

findings.title: CommitIntent: the duration renders as hours ('600:00:00' for 25 days), which is hard to read.
findings.evidence: cases/0.json: duration 2160000 shows as 'Duration 600:00:00'. Descriptor: `format: duration`.
findings.fix: None in the spec today. A days-capable duration rendering would help.

findings.title: CommitIntent: the tokens are paid by whoever submits, and anyone may submit the intent before the deadline.
findings.evidence: CommitmentVaultV5.commitWithSig: `token.safeTransferFrom(msg.sender, address(this), intent.amount);`. NatSpec: 'Anyone can call; the resulting commitment is always owned by intent.user.'
findings.fix: Optionally say in the intent that a relayer submits this using the deposit-address funds.

summary.worst: CommitIntent: 'Stake amount' shows the gross deposit, but the platform fee is cut before the stake is locked.

findings.format: CommitIntent(address user,address token,uint256 amount,bytes32 rulesHash,uint64 duration,uint256 fine,address recipient,uint256 nonce,uint256 deadline)
findings.title: CommitIntent: 'Stake amount' shows the gross deposit, but the platform fee is cut before the stake is locked.
findings.reason: The code keeps the fee for the treasury and locks only totalDeposit minus the fee as the stake. That net stake is what Returned and emergency withdraw pay back, but the screen shows the gross 10 USDC as 'Stake amount' and never mentions a fee. This is the guide's amount rule: a fee rate from storage cuts the amount shown, so it is critical and not the not-critical item 3 (storage values). Also, in case 0 the fine is 10 USDC, which is more than the net stake, so that signed intent would revert with InvalidFine.
findings.quote: CommitmentVaultV4._commit: `uint256 fee = _computeFee(token, totalDeposit); ... uint256 netStake = totalDeposit - fee; if (fine > netStake) revert InvalidFine(fine, netStake); ... _storeCommitment(..., netStake, fine, fee, ...); _credit(token, treasury, fee);` and `_computeFee`: `bpsFee = (totalDeposit * platformFeeBps) / 10_000` (platformFeeBps = 100 in the constructor), with minFeeInToken as the floor. CommitmentVaultV5.commitWithSig passes `received` (the full intent.amount) as totalDeposit. Descriptor: field `amount` labelled 'Stake amount' (tokenAmount); the intent 'Open commitment' and no other field mention a fee. Case 0 screen: 'Stake amount 10 USDC'.

findings.format: CommitIntent(address user,address token,uint256 amount,bytes32 rulesHash,uint64 duration,uint256 fine,address recipient,uint256 nonce,uint256 deadline)
findings.title: CommitIntent: 'Stake amount' shows the gross deposit, but the platform fee is cut before the stake is locked.
findings.reason: Successful commitments lock and refund the deposit minus the platform fee, while the screen labels the gross deposit “Stake amount” without disclosing the deduction. However, case 0 does not demonstrate a successful deduction: its fine equals the deposit, so any positive fee makes it revert.
